decision: Partition the system as an FPGA-first prototype shell around an external GPU/CPU surrogate service. Keep the NVIDIA DoMINO surrogate in gpu_service/software because the qualification is only provisional, inference was not executed, and there is no evidence it is hardware-deployable into RTL. Implement geometry ingestion, surrogate execution, reference computation, verification, and architecture optimization in software/CPU-GPU services; implement command safety, freshness checks, timeout handling, clamping, fallback, and compact transport in FPGA RTL/firmware-facing logic.
decision_factors: Selected model is provisionally compatible only; inference was not executed and accuracy is not qualified.
The chosen surrogate explicitly requires a GPU worker and remote NIM runtime, so it stays in gpu_service/software.
The architecture assigns only bounded transport, safety monitoring, timeout handling, and clamping to FPGA RTL.
The contract requires a transparent reference path, which aligns with CPU software for reproducibility and traceability.
The application requires stale-data rejection, timeout fallback, and actuator clamping, all of which are deterministic safety functions suitable for FPGA.
No evidence in the contract or qualification proves the surrogate is hardware-deployable into ASIC/FPGA.
The implementation path is fpga_prototype, so the hardware role is a safety shell plus compact interfaces, not the physics model itself.

jobs.latency_budget: interactive; preprocessing completes before control-loop submission
jobs.rationale: Geometry parsing and STL validation are software-friendly and not hardware-deployable from the supplied evidence.
jobs.responsibility: Load STL geometry, validate format, normalize DrivAerML-derived inputs, and prepare compact descriptors for downstream use.

jobs.rationale: Envelope validation, metadata packaging, and sequence management are transparent CPU tasks and should stay outside RTL.
jobs.responsibility: Prepare scenario inputs across 20-55 m/s, attach timestamps and sequence IDs, and enforce envelope checks before model submission.

jobs.latency_budget: bounded service latency; must fit within control timeout budget
jobs.rationale: The selected model requires a GPU worker and remote NIM runtime; no evidence supports RTL or FPGA deployment.
jobs.responsibility: Execute the provisionally compatible NVIDIA DoMINO automotive aero surrogate and return model outputs with quality indicators.

jobs.latency_budget: bounded to verification and regression workflow; not on the critical actuator path
jobs.rationale: The architecture explicitly reserves the reference path for transparent software-based validation and comparison.
jobs.responsibility: Run the transparent analytical reference path for traceability, comparison, and verification against the surrogate-driven implementation.

jobs.latency_budget: control-cycle bounded; must complete before watchdog expiry
jobs.rationale: Decision synthesis depends on external model outputs and is not justified as hardware-deployable in the supplied evidence.
jobs.responsibility: Convert surrogate outputs and operating conditions into active-aerodynamics control recommendations.

jobs.rationale: The architecture and RTL spec explicitly assign freshness checks, clamping, and safety gating to the FPGA shell.
jobs.responsibility: Reject stale commands, validate sequence correlation, clamp outputs to safe bounds, and gate actuator release.

jobs.latency_budget: must assert fallback within configured timeout budget
jobs.rationale: Timeout and fallback are hard safety functions that belong in the bounded control shell.
jobs.responsibility: Monitor request age, detect missing or late responses, and force a safe fallback state on timeout or invalid data.

jobs.rationale: Partitioning and optimization are orchestration tasks best handled in software, especially with a provisional model qualification.
jobs.responsibility: Define functional boundaries, map workloads to FPGA/GPU/CPU/software, and optimize the implementation architecture and interfaces.

jobs.rationale: Acceptance gates require measurable validation; test execution and reporting are software tasks with traceability needs.
jobs.responsibility: Run regression tests across the validated velocity range, compare implementation against the reference path, and record compliance results.

jobs.latency_budget: milliseconds; deterministic enough for control supervision
jobs.rationale: The architecture calls for compact register-mapped control/status integration, which is naturally firmware-facing.
jobs.responsibility: Bridge host control software to the FPGA CSR window, move compact metadata, and expose status/faults to supervisory software.

tradeoffs: Keeping surrogate inference in GPU/software preserves flexibility and avoids overcommitting to an unqualified model, but introduces service latency and integration complexity.
Implementing safety logic in FPGA improves determinism and fault containment, but limits on-device intelligence to control gating rather than full physics inference.
Using a CPU transparent reference path improves auditability and regression quality, but it is not intended for real-time actuation.
Compact register/stream interfaces reduce I/O complexity and fit the architecture, but they require careful metadata design instead of bulk payload transport.
A firmware bridge simplifies bring-up and observability, but it adds another layer to maintain between host software and FPGA safety logic.
